title: Flux Rectifier
pages: Craft the Flux Rectifier with gold, copper, one platinum ingot (forge:ingots/platinum), and Purified Salts in the three marked slots. Its Charged Capacitor recipe yields Rectified Filament, and its forming recipe turns a Rectifier Diode Blank into a Germanium Point-Contact Rectifier; the Polarity Inverter needs one of each. The Capacitor Array and Leaching Vat supply both inputs before the Electrolyzer.

Place a gold block directly beneath the controller and a dropper directly above it. Put iron trapdoors on all four horizontal sides at controller height. At dropper height, add copper blocks east and west and redstone blocks north and south: this upper bus supplies the two contact rails and polarity pair. Any missing or swapped contact, side, cap or base stops operation. Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded flux_rectification recipe. It loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. It needs no FE; hand use and the automation buffer below share the same recipes.

It runs 21 exclusive datapack flux_rectification recipes: 19 reclaim useful stock from spent rails, minecarts and signal parts, while two form Rectified Filament and the Germanium Point-Contact Rectifier. Six activator rails return four iron bars; six detector rails return two chains; chest, furnace, hopper and TNT minecarts yield their matching cargo. Two lanterns yield four iron nuggets, two soul lanterns one soul torch, four note blocks two redstone torches, and six powered rails eight gold nuggets, and two redstone lamps two glowstone dust. Other batches reclaim iron, gold, redstone or quartz at a loss. These outputs support signal wiring, lighting and cart assembly without duplicating every batch as an ingot. Two Charged Capacitors from the Capacitor Array form one Rectified Filament. One Rectifier Diode Blank (Sawmill germanium wafer, copper contact whisker, porcelain insulator) becomes a one-way Germanium Point-Contact Rectifier. Five chains recover two iron ingots; two iron bars make one chain in the hot press, so the loop loses iron. Three repeaters recover two redstone; annealing one redstone gives one torch and relaying four torches gives two repeaters, so that loop also loses dust.

The Rectified Filament and the Germanium Point-Contact Rectifier are both consumed by the Polarity Inverter controller craft, and the filament also feeds Stator Coil polarity inversion. With JEI installed, search the Flux Rectifier controller for the Flux Rectification category; it shows every loaded recipe, exact batch counts and formation requirements.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded flux rectification recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
